messages.content: Now that Hotel Folly is booked, I need to settle the drive from Dallas. Compare stopping in Birmingham with pushing to the Atlanta outskirts. There are three of us, and I want realistic days, not map times that assume we never stop.

Dallas to the Charleston coast is roughly 1,080 miles and about 16 hours of wheel time before fuel, meals, traffic, and the one-hour time change. Birmingham makes the split about 640 miles on day one and 450-470 on day two. A west-Atlanta stop makes day one roughly 770-790 miles, leaving about 320-340 miles the next day. With normal breaks, Birmingham is about a 10.5-hour first day; west Atlanta is closer to 12.5-13 hours.
Put that against our July 12 check-in. What time would we need to leave Dallas on the 11th, and when would each option get us to Hotel Folly?

For Birmingham, leaving Dallas at 7:00 a.m. Central on July 11 should put you at a suburban hotel around 5:00-5:30 p.m. Central after lunch, fuel, and two shorter breaks. Leave Birmingham around 7:30 a.m. Central on July 12 and you should reach Hotel Folly around 4:00-4:30 p.m. Eastern, allowing for stops and the time-zone change. For west Atlanta, a 6:30 a.m. Dallas departure would likely mean a 7:00-7:30 p.m. Eastern arrival near Lithia Springs or Douglasville. Leaving there at 9:00 a.m. would put you at the coast around 3:00 p.m., subject to Atlanta and Charleston traffic.
So Atlanta gets us there earlier on check-in day, but at the cost of a much worse first day.

Correct. It gains roughly an hour to an hour and a half on July 12, but adds about 140 miles and two to two and a half hours to July 11. It also exposes the longer day to evening traffic on the west side of Atlanta. Birmingham produces two more balanced stages and reaches the property close to a typical afternoon check-in window.
Give me representative hotel numbers for both places. One room, two queen beds, all three registered, parking included. We do not need anything upscale for a road night.

For planning rather than a live reservation, a two-queen room at a Hampton Inn, Fairfield, or Holiday Inn Express in Hoover or Trussville is reasonably budgeted at $145-$175 after tax, generally with free parking and breakfast. On the west Atlanta side, comparable properties around Lithia Springs are more often about $155-$190 after tax, also commonly including parking and breakfast. I would carry $165 for Birmingham and $175 for west Atlanta until exact July 11 inventory and occupancy terms are checked.
What about fuel for the whole round trip? Our vehicle gets about 25 miles per gallon on highway trips.

Using about 2,160 route miles for a Birmingham round trip, the vehicle would use roughly 86.4 gallons. At a planning price of $3.20 per gallon, that is about $276. Add $15-$25 for local driving, traffic, or a detour, so $300 is a sensible fuel allowance. Routing through west Atlanta in one or both directions would add only a modest fuel amount, roughly $10-$20 per Atlanta leg, but the bigger cost is time.
I also want the return mapped out. We check out July 18. Could we leave after breakfast, stop in Birmingham again, and still get home at a reasonable hour the next day?

Yes. If you leave Hotel Folly at 9:00 a.m. Eastern on July 18, allow about eight hours including lunch and fuel, then gain an hour crossing into Central Time. That puts you in the Birmingham area around 4:00-4:30 p.m. Central. Leaving Birmingham at 7:00 a.m. Central on July 19 should put you in Dallas around 5:00-5:30 p.m. after normal breaks.
Would taking the Atlanta stop on the return make any sense, perhaps to keep the first day shorter after checkout?

It would make July 18 easier: Charleston to west Atlanta is roughly 330 miles, around six hours with stops, so a 9:00 a.m. departure could reach the hotel near 3:00 p.m. Eastern. The tradeoff is July 19, when you would face about 770 miles and roughly 12-13 hours with breaks to Dallas. It shifts the hard day rather than reducing it, and the hard day comes at the end of the vacation.
No, I do not want a 13-hour final day. Use Birmingham in both directions. Which side of Birmingham is practical so we are not adding city traffic in the morning?

Hoover, along I-459 south of central Birmingham, is the practical target in both directions. It keeps you near the through route, has many chain hotels and restaurants, and avoids using a downtown hotel or paying downtown parking. Trussville can work, but it is less convenient for the Dallas-to-Charleston routing and can add local mileage.
Build the road budget with two Hoover hotel nights, fuel, and a little room for tolls or parking. Keep meals separate because we would buy those at home too.

Using $165 per Hoover night, lodging is $330. Fuel is budgeted at $300. The standard Birmingham route does not require meaningful toll spending, but a $20 road contingency covers incidental parking, route changes, or small price differences. That makes the transportation and roadside-lodging plan $650, excluding meals. If both hotels include breakfast and free parking, there should be no additional overnight-property cost.
Can you lay out the exact schedule we are choosing, including time zones? I want to send it to my spouse without having to explain the clock changes.

Outbound: leave Dallas Friday, July 11, at 7:00 a.m. Central; arrive in Hoover around 5:00-5:30 p.m. Central; stay one night. Leave Hoover Saturday, July 12, at 7:30 a.m. Central; arrive at Hotel Folly around 4:00-4:30 p.m. Eastern. Return: leave Hotel Folly Friday, July 18, at 9:00 a.m. Eastern; arrive in Hoover around 4:00-4:30 p.m. Central; stay one night. Leave Hoover Saturday, July 19, at 7:00 a.m. Central; arrive home in Dallas around 5:00-5:30 p.m. Central.
That works. Select the Hoover plan but do not reserve the roadside rooms yet. Note what has to be checked when we price them.

The selected plan is Hoover in both directions, with unbooked rooms for July 11 and July 18. Price one two-queen room each night for two adults and one 14-year-old, and verify that all three guests are registered, parking is free, breakfast is included for three, the quoted total includes tax, and the cancellation deadline is acceptable. Use properties close to I-459 and avoid any option that materially lengthens the route. The working road budget is $650: $330 for two hotel nights, $300 fuel, and a $20 contingency, with meals excluded.
